# Hybrid Pi Dispatch: Pane When in a Herdr Session, Headless Fallback Otherwise

## Problem statement

The evaluation of Pi subprocess mechanisms (discovered-from:WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7) found that /skill:audit is dispatched two ways: user-initiated audits open a visible herdr pi pane via send-to-pi.sh, while automated contexts (heartbeat, cron, CI, ssh) must run headless via `pi -p --mode json`. Currently the choice of mechanism is hard-wired per caller and there is no shared way to get a visible pane when a herdr session exists and fall back to a headless subprocess when it does not. The podcast editor (open_source_llm/experimental/herdr-podcast-editor) already implements exactly this hybrid pattern via a HERDR_ENV check; it is a proven precedent to generalise.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want agent work to be visible whenever a herdr session is present, even when the invocation originates from a script or automated context.
- **Skills authors / plugin authors** — want a single reusable dispatch primitive instead of maintaining two mechanisms.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when an audit is triggered from a context that has a herdr session available, I want it to open in a visible pi pane so I can watch it."
- "As a producer, when no herdr session is available, I want the same invocation to fall back to headless execution so the work still happens."
- "As a plugin author, I want to dispatch a skill to pi once and have it choose pane-vs-headless automatically."

## Expected behaviour

- A shared dispatch helper determines at runtime whether a herdr session/pane environment is available (e.g. HERDR_ENV or herdr CLI/socket presence, mirroring the podcast editor).
- When available: dispatch via send-to-pi.sh (visible pane).
- When unavailable: fall back to `pi -p --mode json` headless execution with the same command.
- Existing callers keep their behaviour; new callers (e.g. heartbeat audits, user-initiated audits outside the worklist) opt in.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Add the helper to the shared herdr scripts (packages/herdr/shared/) and/or a small skill-level utility so both herdr code and skills can use it.
- Model the fallback on the podcast editor's send-to-pi.sh wrapper + direct-subprocess branch.
- Wire the heartbeat audit dispatch to use the hybrid helper (pane when herdr present, headless otherwise), which also delivers visibility (see WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A shared dispatch helper exists that selects pane vs headless at runtime based on herdr availability.
2. With a herdr environment present, dispatch opens a visible pi pane running the given command.
3. Without a herdr environment, dispatch runs the command headless via `pi -p --mode json` and returns programmatic output.
4. At least one existing caller (e.g. heartbeat audit dispatch) is converted to use the helper without regressing its current behaviour.
5. Tests cover both branches (herdr present / absent).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Show plugin version in Herdr work item selection list (WL-0MSGKEBFU004T3N3)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Worklog work item selection list gives no indication of which plugin version is running, making it hard to verify installs, spot stale builds, or report bugs accurately. A dimmed, right-aligned version number in the pane header solves this without visual clutter.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who want to confirm which version of the Worklog Selection List plugin is running.
- **Developers/support** who need the version handy when filing bug reports or verifying an updated build is live.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the plugin version in the corner of the work item list, so I can confirm which build I'm running.
- As a developer, I want the version visible but unobtrusive, so it doesn't distract from the list content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The work item selection list header shows the plugin version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json`), right-aligned to the pane width.
2. The version is rendered in the dimmed ANSI style (`\x1b[2m`), matching the existing `[auto-refresh on]` treatment, and does not interfere with the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title.
3. The version is read at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` (not hardcoded in the renderer), so it stays in sync with the manifest version.
4. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover the header rendering with the version suffix, including a case without a version available (graceful fallback).
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Unobtrusive: dimmed font, right-aligned to the pane edge; must not change existing header content or alignment of the title.
- Use existing patterns: `termSize.cols` for pane width, `ANSI.dim` for dimming, `readFileSync` for reading `package.json` (pattern already used in `worklist.ts`/`shortcut-config.ts`).
- No changes to `herdr-plugin.toml` version unless a version bump is explicitly requested.
- Do not update CHANGELOG.md (managed automatically by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Existing state

- The selection list header is rendered in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (~line 1585): ` Work Items — N item(s)` plus optional `[auto-refresh on]` (dimmed) and `[paused — hidden]` indicators.
- `termSize` (with `cols`) is available in the render function; `truncateLine()` handles width overflow.
- The plugin version is declared in two places: `packages/herdr/package.json` (`"version": "0.1.0"`) and `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` (`version = "0.1.0"`). There is currently no runtime version constant.
- Existing header tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (lines ~86–100) assert `'Work Items'` presence.

## Desired change

1. Add a runtime helper that reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (e.g., parse JSON, fall back to a safe default like `'?'` or omit when unreadable).
2. In the list-mode header renderer, append a dimmed `v<version>` string right-aligned to `cols` (using padding), while keeping the title left-aligned.
3. Add unit tests covering: version suffix present and right-aligned, dim style applied, graceful fallback when the version can't be read.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Header rendering; add version read + right-aligned dimmed suffix (near line 1585).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Header assertions for version suffix, alignment, and fallback.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — Version source (`0.1.0`); no change expected.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Optional: document the version display.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Create a work item selection list in Herdr: parent feature that produced `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **WL-0MQHYI4E60075SQT** — Fix icon prefix alignment in Pi TUI work item selection list: related header/line formatting work (Pi TUI counterpart).
- **WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ** — Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus: related Herdr list behavior work.
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** — Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension: related footer/status UI precedent (Pi TUI counterpart).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKX5ZV3D0OHIIX2** – Add regression tests for mouse click crash and TUI behavior (completed)
- **WL-0MKZ34IDI0XTA5TB** – TUI: Reparent items without typing IDs (completed)
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** – Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, src, using, version, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2-enforce-git-worktree-usage-for-all-imple/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: `package.json` is present next to the compiled/tsx module at runtime; the module-dir relative read pattern (as in `shortcut-config.ts`) works for both `npx tsx` and `dist` runs.
- **Risk**: ANSI codes in a right-padded line can misalign padding calculations if padding is computed on raw text length; must compute visible-width padding before applying ANSI styles.
- **Risk**: Very narrow panes could crowd the header; the version suffix should be dropped or truncated if it would overlap the title (guard on `cols`).
- **Scope creep risk**: Bumping the version, adding the version elsewhere (footer/status bar), or showing `wl`/ContextHub versions — out of scope; record as follow-up work items if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: "Which version number? I assume the plugin's own version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json` / `herdr-plugin.toml`) — or did you mean the `wl` CLI version or ContextHub's version?"  
  **Answer** (user): "yes the plugins" — the Worklog Selection List plugin's own version. Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2**: "Placement preference? Unobtrusive, dimmed — candidates: (a) right side of the header line, (b) footer hint line, (c) bottom-right corner."  
  **Answer** (user): "a (right aligned to width of pane)" — right-aligned in the header line. Source: interactive reply.

# Objective

Make the worklog-selection-list plugin's chord shortcuts **extensible per project**: the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` provides the default chords, and a **project-local `shortcuts.json`** (discovered from the resolved worklog root) provides additional entries and overrides. Today `loadShortcutConfig()` reads only the bundled file, so projects cannot add project-specific chords without forking the plugin.

## Problem statement

A consuming project (open_source_llm) needs a `w` chord that dispatches `/skill:wiki-podcast-script --doc <path> --force-single` / `--rewrite <path>` to a pi agent pane for podcast episode work items. That chord is project-specific and must **not** be added to the core plugin's bundled `shortcuts.json` (operator decision). The plugin currently loads shortcuts exclusively from `join(__dirname, 'shortcuts.json')` (see `loadShortcutConfig()` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts`), so there is no supported way to add or override chords per project.

## Users

Herdr users of the worklog-selection-list plugin, and projects that consume it (e.g. open_source_llm's podcast production workflow).

- As a plugin user, I want the plugin's built-in chords (c, n, p, i, r, s, …) to remain available by default, so I can keep the standard workflow unchanged.
- As a project maintainer, I want to add project-specific chords (e.g. `w` → write podcast script) in a local file without editing the plugin source, so upgrades/rebuilds of the plugin do not lose my chords.
- As a project maintainer, I want a local chord with the same key sequence as a bundled one to override the bundled behavior, so I can tailor defaults per project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `loadShortcutConfig()` loads the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` as before (backward compatible; no local file → identical behavior to today).
- [ ] When a project-local `shortcuts.json` exists, its entries are merged: new chords are added, and a local entry whose chord sequence (+ view) matches a bundled entry overrides it (local wins). Override semantics are documented and unit-tested.
- [ ] The project-local file is resolved relative to the **worklog root** (the root that `configureWorklogTarget()` / `resolveWorklogRoot()` resolves from `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, i.e. the directory containing `.worklog/`), so the same plugin install serves different chords in different projects.
- [ ] Local file location and merge order are documented in the plugin README (config section), including the override rule and validation behavior.
- [ ] Malformed local entries are logged and skipped without breaking the bundled defaults (same defensive posture as the bundled parser; invalid values never crash or hide shortcuts).
- [ ] Existing chord behavior is unchanged when no local file is present; full `npm test` suite (shortcut-config tests and others) passes.

## Design notes / open questions

- **Local file location:** proposal is `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json` (next to `.worklog/`). Alternative: a hidden name (`.herdr/shortcuts.json` or `.pi/shortcuts.json`) to avoid a bare `shortcuts.json` in the project root. The worklog root already has `.worklog/`; a `shortcuts.json` next to it is simple and discoverable. Confirm which location is preferred (see Open Questions).
- **Override key:** chord sequence + view (`'list'|'detail'|'both'`) is the natural key. A local entry with the same chord+view replaces the bundled entry; same chord with a different view coexists. A local `stages` filter narrows availability (already supported by `ShortcutEntry`).
- **Merge mechanics:** `loadShortcutConfig()` currently takes no arguments. Extend it to accept the resolved worklog root (or read `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`), parse both files, and merge (bundled first, local appended/overriding). The registry already de-duplicates by exact lookup; explicit override handling must be added so duplicate chords do not produce ambiguous lookups (`lookupChordEntry` uses `entries.find` — the first match wins, so local entries must replace bundled ones at the same key, not just be appended).
- **`code_freeze`:** local entries may carry `code_freeze` like bundled ones (parser already supports it); no extra work expected.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `loadShortcutConfig()` merge logic, override handling, optional local-path argument.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — new tests: no-local-file (identical defaults), local adds new chord, local overrides bundled, malformed local entry skipped, per-project resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the resolved worklog root into `loadShortcutConfig()` (note: `loadShortcutConfig()` is currently called before `configureWorklogTarget()` in `main()`; the call order or plumbing must be adjusted so the local file is found).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the local `shortcuts.json` convention, merge/override rules, and location.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh` — no change expected (already passes `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`); confirm.

## Related work

- Consuming work item (open_source_llm worklog): **Add 'w' chord to write podcast script in ContextHub worklist plugin (OSL-0MSHFQ51L009IUOS)** — needs this extensibility to add its `w` chord without touching the plugin's bundled shortcuts.
- **Model selection per shortcut (WL-0MSD48ZFC0043AO3)** — added the `model` field to shortcut entries; the local-config extension must preserve it (parser already handles it).
- **Code-freeze shortcut visibility (WL-0MSD81VEL009XHWA)** — added `code_freeze` to shortcut entries; preserved by the same parser.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the project-local file should live at the worklog root (or a documented sub-path there) so the plugin can find it with the already-resolved root; exact name to be confirmed.
- **Risk:** duplicate chord sequences between bundled and local files must be resolved deterministically (local wins) or `entries.find` will silently pick the bundled one. Explicit override logic + tests mitigate.
- **Risk (scope creep):** full user-level config files (per-user, per-host), hot-reload of shortcuts, and UI for editing shortcuts are out of scope; track separately if requested.
- **Compatibility:** projects with no local file must see byte-for-byte identical behavior (guard against regressions).

## Open Questions

- **OPEN QUESTION (eng/producer):** Local file location — `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json` vs `<worklog-root>/.herdr/shortcuts.json` vs `<worklog-root>/.pi/shortcuts.json`? `.pi/settings.json` already exists at the project root of the consuming repo, so `.pi/` has precedent as a project-config location; `.herdr/` is more plugin-scoped. Recommend one and confirm.
- **OPEN QUESTION (eng):** Should the override key be chord+view only, or also stage? (Chord+view is the minimal key; stage is a visibility filter, not an identity.) Recommend chord+view.

# Herdr metadata panel: drop duplicate ID row from data section

## Problem statement

In the herdr work item selection list, the metadata panel for the selected item shows the work item ID twice: once in the panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) and again as the first row of the metadata data table (`ID  WL-XXXX`). The ID row in the data table is redundant and should be dropped, leaving the ID only in the panel title line.

## Users

Users navigating work items in the herdr selection list (`prefix+l`).

**User story:** As a user browsing work items in the herdr selection list, I want the item ID shown once in the metadata panel so the panel is not redundant and the layout is cleaner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The metadata data table in the herdr metadata panel no longer contains an `ID` row.
- [ ] The metadata panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) still shows the item ID.
- [ ] Other metadata rows (Status, Stage, Priority, Title, etc.) render unchanged.
- [ ] The detail view (`formatDetailContent`) behavior is unchanged (it already omits ID/Title from its table since they appear in its header).
- [ ] Tests are added/updated covering the metadata panel output (e.g. the `formatMetadataPanel` describe block in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix should follow the existing pattern used by the detail view (`formatDetailContent` filters `ID`/`Title` out of the table since they are in the header).
- No behavior change to the CLI `show` output or other renderers.

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:

- `formatMetadataPanel` (line ~874) renders the panel header separator `── ${item.id} ──` (line ~891) and then the metadata table from `buildMetaRows(item)` (line ~894).
- `buildMetaRows` (line ~828) unconditionally adds the ID as the first row via `addMeta('ID', item.id)` (line ~835).
- The detail view `formatDetailContent` (line ~969) already filters `ID` and `Title` out of the shared table because both appear in its header: `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID' && label !== 'Title')`.

So the metadata panel currently shows the ID in both the header line and the first data row — the inconsistency with the detail view.

## Desired change

Remove the `ID` row from the metadata table rendered in the metadata panel, consistent with how `formatDetailContent` handles it. The header line `── WL-XXXX ──` continues to display the ID. The `Title` row should remain in the metadata panel table since the panel header does not show the title.

Likely approach: in `formatMetadataPanel`, filter the `ID` row from `buildMetaRows(item)` output (e.g. `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID')`), mirroring `formatDetailContent`. Alternatively, remove `addMeta('ID', item.id)` from `buildMetaRows` — but note `formatDetailContent` relies on `buildMetaRows` including ID then filtering it, so removing it from the shared builder is also safe as long as tests are updated. Prefer the filter-in-panel approach for minimal blast radius.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel` (~line 874) and/or `buildMetaRows` (~line 828); the ID row is added at line ~835.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel — field rendering and scrolling` describe block (~line 896); add a test asserting the data table no longer contains an `ID` row while the header still shows the ID. Existing test `expect(joined).toContain('WL-RICH1')` may still pass via the header, but a negative assertion is needed.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** — "Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command" (completed): introduced the metadata panel and shared `buildMetaRows` (origin of the ID duplication).
- **WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9** — "Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section" (open): also touches metadata section presentation.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** — "Show description preview in herder plugin selection list" (open): related to the selection list metadata area.
- **WL-0MNK7CB3F0008YT3** — "Display work item ID in TUI metadata block" (completed): the deprecated Blessed-TUI predecessor; closed as wont-fix/deprecated — not to be used as a pattern.

(Note: an automated find-related scan flagged WL-0MQCU6R6V008JX62, WL-0MRERDU1J000W1IS, WL-0MM0DBM6I1PHQBFI and README worktree copies; these were false positives from keyword overlap and are not genuinely related — excluded per conservative policy.)

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "metadata section" refers to the herdr selection-list metadata panel (the only place showing the ID both in a title line and as the first data-table row). The CLI `show` output shows ID once in its metadata table with no separate ID-bearing title line, so it is out of scope.
- Low risk: change is localized; detail view and CLI outputs are unaffected.
- Scope creep: do not change icon consistency (tracked by WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9) or add description previews (tracked by WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3) in this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which metadata section is this about?" — Answer (user): "The metadata section has the ID in the title line and in the first line of the data section. Drop it from the data section." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: the herdr metadata panel, whose title line is `── <id> ──` and whose first data-table row is `ID  <id>`. Verified against `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (lines 891 and 835).
- Q: "Should the Title row remain in the metadata panel table?" — Assumption (agent, Map): Yes — the panel header shows only the ID, not the title, so Title is not duplicated and stays. Source: code inspection of `formatMetadataPanel` header (line 891 shows only `item.id`). Documented in Desired change.
data.title: Herdr metadata panel: drop duplicate ID row from data section

# Intake Brief: Colour code work items by priority in selection lists (CLI + Herdr)

**Work Item ID:** WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6

**Headline:** Colour coding of work items in the selection list should be based on **priority**, not stage: critical are red, low are dimmed, medium is white, high is orange — recorded in a shared theme file.

## Problem Statement

Work item titles in selection lists are currently coloured by **stage** (progression: gray → blue → cyan → yellow → green → white, from WL-0MQ53H78W000DQ08). Stage progression communicates workflow position, but operators scanning a list need to see **priority** at a glance — critical items should jump out in red, low-priority items should recede. The colour scheme must be defined once in a shared theme file.

## Users

All Worklog users viewing work item lists:

- **Operators and agents** scanning `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent` need immediate visual cue of what matters (critical = red, high = orange).
- **Herdr users** browsing the Worklog selection list pane need the same priority cue.

Example user stories:
- "As an operator, I want critical work items to appear red so I can immediately spot what needs attention."
- "As an agent, I want low-priority items dimmed so they recede while scanning the list."
- "As a project manager, I want a consistent priority colour scheme across the CLI and the Herdr selection list, defined in one shared theme file."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The canonical priority colour mapping is recorded in the shared theme file `src/theme.ts`:
   - `critical` → red
   - `high` → orange
   - `medium` → white
   - `low` → dimmed
2. Work item **titles** are coloured by priority and work item **ids** are coloured by stage, everywhere they appear: `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl recent`, `wl show`, `wl next`, and the Herdr worklist selection list (`formatItemLine`).
3. Blocked items no longer receive the unconditional red override; they are coloured by their natural priority like every other item (per clarification Q3b).
4. Unknown/missing priority falls back to a sensible default colour (e.g. medium/white) and unknown/missing stage keeps a sensible default (gray) — matching current fallback behaviour.
5. Unit tests cover the new priority colour mapping and the title/priority + id/stage split in both the CLI helpers (`src/commands/helpers.ts`) and the Herdr icons (`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`), including blocked and unknown-priority cases.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr/`) is a separate package depending only on `@worklog/shared`; it renders raw ANSI 256-colour escape codes and cannot import `src/theme.ts` (which depends on chalk).
- The Pi-based TUI extension (`packages/tui/`) is **out of scope** — it is slated for removal (see WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N) and colours via Pi theme tokens, not the theme file.
- "Orange" should use a colour consistent with the existing `theme.text.readyNo` (`chalk.hex('#FFA500')`).
- No new dependencies.

# Auto-downgrade critical priority when item is marked completed/in_review

## Problem statement

A work item that is marked **completed/in_review** can still carry `critical` priority today. Critical is a signal for urgent *open* work — it drives `wl next` ordering, TUI selection lists, and grouping — so a finished item left at critical competes with genuinely urgent items and makes dashboards misleading. When an item transitions to a terminal state (`status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`), its priority must not remain `critical`.

## Users

- **Operators and agents** who close out work items.
  - *As an operator, when I mark a critical item as completed/in_review, I want its priority automatically downgraded to `high`, so that finished work stops competing with genuinely urgent open items.*
  - *As a developer, I want the automatic downgrade reported in the command output, so that I can verify the change happened.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state — `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` (via `wl update`) or `status=completed` (via `wl close`) — its priority is automatically downgraded to `high`.
2. Priorities other than `critical` (`high`, `medium`, `low`) are never modified by a terminal transition.
3. Command output reports the downgrade: a machine-readable field in `--json` output and a summary line in human-readable output, consistent with the existing `downgradedChildren` reporting in `wl update`.
4. Unit tests cover: `wl update --status completed`, `wl update --stage in_review`, `wl close`, and no-op cases (non-critical priorities unchanged; non-terminal transitions like `plan_complete` leave `critical` intact).
5. Full project test suite passes, and `CLI.md` documentation for `wl update` / `wl close` is updated to describe the auto-downgrade behavior.

## Constraints

- Canonical priorities are `critical | high | medium | low` (see `src/validators/priority.ts`); the downgrade target is `high` per operator specification.
- Only terminal transitions trigger the downgrade — moving `critical` items between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must not touch priority.
- Must not conflict with the existing child cascade: `cascadePriorityDowngrade` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (parent downgrade → children). A completed item is itself terminal, so no child cascade is implied by this rule.
- Prefer reusing existing reporting patterns from `src/commands/update.ts` over inventing new output formats.

## Existing state

- The database allows any priority with any status/stage; there is no rule preventing `critical` on completed/in_review items today.
- Terminal transitions are: `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (`src/commands/update.ts`) and `wl close <id>` (`src/commands/close.ts` sets `status=completed`, `stage=done`).
- A directly related cascade already exists: `cascadePriorityDowngrade(parentId, newPriority)` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (line ~1230) downgrades critical *children* to `high` when a parent drops from `critical`, reported via `downgradedChildren` in `src/commands/update.ts` (lines ~383–408).
- `wl doctor` validates status/stage combinations (`src/doctor/status-stage-check.ts`) but has no priority-vs-stage rule.

## Desired change

1. Add a small helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal(updatedItem)` or an inline check alongside the existing cascade) that, when an item is transitioning to a terminal state, downgrades `critical` → `high`.
2. Invoke it from the terminal-transition paths in `src/commands/update.ts` (stage/status changes) and `src/commands/close.ts` (close path). Decide between explicit call sites vs. enforcement inside the shared `update()` — prefer explicit call sites to avoid side effects on internal cascade `update()` calls unless a guard makes it safe.
3. Report downgraded items in JSON and human-readable output, mirroring the `downgradedChildren` pattern.
4. Add unit tests and update `CLI.md`.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling (`--status completed` / `--stage in_review`); add downgrade enforcement and reporting.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path sets `status=completed`; enforce downgrade here too.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — home of `cascadePriorityDowngrade`; natural location for the new helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal`) if a DB-layer helper is preferred.
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — canonical priority constants to reuse.
- `tests/database.test.ts` (and/or `tests/cli/*`) — unit tests for the new behavior.
- `CLI.md` — document auto-downgrade in `wl update` / `wl close` sections.

## Related work

- `Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced (WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR)` — completed; the direct precedent: same `critical` → `high` downgrade rule and reporting pattern, but for parent→child cascades.
- `Add priority normalization to create, update and doctor commands (WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G)` — completed; priority validation infrastructure (`src/validators/priority.ts`).
- `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` — completed; critical-priority semantics in `wl next`.
- `Exclude in-review items from wl next (WL-0ML2TS8I409ALBU6)` — completed; in_review semantics.
- `Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added (WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6)` — open; sibling rule about terminal-state invariants on parents.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** `wl doctor` detection/fix of legacy `critical` + completed/in_review items is a natural extension but is NOT part of this work item's ACs. If wanted, record as a separate linked work item (`discovered-from:WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9`).
- **Over-enforcement risk:** blanket enforcement inside the shared DB `update()` could interfere with internal calls (e.g., the child cascade calls `db.update()`); guard conditions must be precise or enforcement kept at explicit call sites.
- **Assumption:** "completed/in_review" means terminal transitions — `status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`, plus `stage=done` via `wl close`.
- **Assumption:** the downgrade target is `high`, as explicitly specified by the operator.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: The request ended with `--priority low` — what does it refer to?
  - A (assumed, rgardler): `--priority low` sets the priority of this new work item itself (matching `wl create --priority low` CLI syntax), not the downgrade target — the feature spec explicitly downgrades to `high`. Source: interactive reply; interpretation documented here. If wrong, the item priority is a one-line `wl update` fix.
- No further clarification was needed; the seed context was sufficient to draft the brief (interview skipped per intake skill step 4).

# Feature Request: --fields field-selection for wl list / wl search

## Problem statement

wl list and wl search return full work-item records (or compact snippets for search), with no way to request only the fields a caller needs. Full-record dumps are the root cause of token waste documented in SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents): bare wl list --json = 5.3 MB / 1,861 records; wl list --status completed = 4.9 MB; scripts (ship gates, triage, code-review) download tens-to-hundreds of KB of fields they never read (e.g. full descriptions) when they only need id, title, status, stage, priority.

## User stories

- As a release-gate script, I want wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title,status,stage,needsProducerReview --json so I stop downloading 4.9 MB of descriptions I discard.
- As an agent running /skill:audit, I want a compact project-status query (fields id,title,status,stage,priority) so the worklog overview stays in the low-KB range.
- As a triage helper, I want wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --fields id,title,description --json so my match heuristics get exactly the fields they need.

## Expected behaviour

- New option on wl list and wl search: --fields comma-separated (e.g. id,title,status,stage,priority).
- Output objects contain ONLY the requested fields (plus id always, for usability); unknown field names are rejected with a clear error listing valid fields.
- wl list and wl search share the same field vocabulary: id, title, description, status, stage, priority, issueType, assignee, tags, createdAt, updatedAt, parentId, needsProducerReview, sortIndex.
- --json output shape unchanged (same keys; omitted fields absent). Human output uses the same projection for concise display.
- -f as shorthand is acceptable; must not clash with existing flags (-F/--format already taken).

## Acceptance criteria

1. wl list --fields id,title --json returns objects with only id/title; verified for filters and bare queries.
2. wl search term --fields id,title,status --json returns compact objects with only those fields.
3. Invalid field names produce a non-zero exit and a clear error listing valid fields.
4. Output size reduction verified: wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title --json is smaller than the full-record equivalent (target: >=90% reduction for the completed-status case cited above).
5. Existing output without --fields is unchanged (backward compatible); full test suite passes.

4. Scope sizing: Small effort, Low risk - appropriate for scope.

## Plan Changelog

- 2026-08-23T09:09Z - Plan created with 5 child work items. Pre-check: Small effort, Low risk. All review stages passed.

- Q: Should --fields support nested field access (e.g. auditResult.readyToClose)? Answer (plan agent): No. The work item scope is flat field selection only. Nested access can be added later if needed. Final: not in scope.
- Q: Should -f shorthand be supported? Answer (plan agent): Yes, but -f is not taken in either list or search. Final: -f can be added as shorthand.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, when the local LLM is idle, I want the herdr downtime
worker to avoid starting **non-critical** implementations while the
completed/in_review review queue is already deep enough to fill the
selection list, so the producer-review bottleneck is not overloaded.
Auditing, intake, and planning can still be dispatched — only the
implement tier is gated.

## Background

- Dispatch tier order (dispatchDowntimeWork): scheduled prompts → audit →
  implement → plan → intake. The code-freeze gate (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY)
  already skips audit+implement during a release; this is a second,
  orthogonal implement-tier-only throttle on the producer-review queue.
- The herdr selection list displays up to `browseItemCount` items
  (default 20, clamp 1–50, packages/herdr/src/settings.ts).
- Review-queue count = completed/in_review **root** items
  (`wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json`) —
  same query family as the audit tier (WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG) and the
  selection list's mandatory review subset (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
  Operator decision (2026-08): count is ROOT-ONLY, not all items.
- Implement candidates carry `priority` (critical/high/medium/low) via
  parseImplementCandidatesOutput.

## Design notes

- Gate: when `reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount`, the implement tier
  selects only candidates with `priority === 'critical'`; non-critical
  candidates are excluded and dispatch falls through to plan/intake.
- Critical priority BYPASSES the gate — a critical implement always stays
  eligible regardless of queue depth.
- Fail-closed: a wl error counting the review queue → gate active (only
  critical implements), consistent with the code-freeze "ambiguous ⇒
  frozen" convention.
- `browseItemCount` is re-read live from settings on each dispatch (no
  plugin restart needed), matching the existing config() re-read pattern.
- The gate skip must NOT look like an empty backlog: when implement
  candidates exist but are gated AND plan/intake are empty, the outcome
  must be a neutral reason (never 'no-candidate'), so the worker's
  no-candidate cooldown is not triggered — polling continues and a
  critical implement / new plan / intake item dispatches immediately
  (mirrors the code-freeze 'code-freeze' reason convention).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A critical-priority implement candidate is always eligible regardless
   of review-queue depth (critical bypasses the gate).
2. When reviewQueueCount < browseItemCount, implement-tier selection is
   UNCHANGED: all priorities eligible; risk/effort/dispatched-marker
   filters unchanged.
3. When reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount, non-critical implement
   candidates are excluded; if only non-critical candidates remain,
   getNextImplementCandidate resolves null and dispatch falls through to
   plan/intake (no-candidate only when plan AND intake are genuinely
   empty; a gate skip with an empty plan/intake backlog is a neutral
   reason, never 'no-candidate').
4. The gate applies ONLY to the implement tier — audit, plan, intake,
   and scheduled-prompt dispatch are unaffected.
5. The review-queue count query is bounded by DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS and
   fail-closed (error ⇒ gate active).
6. Tests cover: gate boundary (count == listSize − 1 vs count == listSize),
   critical bypass, root-only counting, fall-through outcome, and the
   neutral (no-cooldown) reason on a gate skip with empty plan/intake.

## Related work

- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — Implement tier end-to-end in herdr downtime worker
- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — Audit tier (completed/in_review without valid audit)
- WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY — Code-freeze gate
- WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B — Selection list must always show all
  completed/in_review and critical items

# Faster downtime dispatch cadence: reduce poll interval and idle threshold

## Problem statement

The downtime worker polls the proxy status every `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (default 10s, hard floor `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS` = 10s) and requires the model to be continuously idle for `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (default 60s, floor 1s) before dispatching. Per dispatch cycle this imposes ~70s of scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn/claim overhead).

During the 04:00-06:00 cheap window (2026-08-22 proxy usage analysis) inter-run gaps of 141s, 146s and 312s were observed between consecutive dispatched runs — a large fraction (est. ~13% of the window) attributable to this threshold+poll+spawn cadence, on top of the model being idle ~50-68% of the time. The current 10s poll floor is a hard-coded guard ("must not hammer the proxy") rather than a measured load limit; the 60s idle threshold is a conservative default from the early worker design.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants more work dispatched into the idle overnight windows; lower latency between dispatch opportunities.
- **Herdr downtime users** — more items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both knobs stay configurable via downtime settings (existing `pollIntervalMs` / `idleThresholdMs` pattern) with **lowered floors**:
   - poll interval floor reduced from 10s to a measured-safe value (target 5s; assert proxy `/llama/local/status` call volume stays negligible — status endpoint is cheap and local);
   - idle threshold floor reduced to ≥1s (current floor) but adjusted production default lowered from 60s to a tuned value (target 15-30s) for the cheap window.
2. Defaults: cheap/downtime mode adopts the faster cadence; interactive or operator-session-sensitive paths unchanged.
3. The idle-gate semantics are preserved: dispatch still only occurs after the model has been continuously idle for the (shorter) threshold — no dispatch into a busy slot, no claim race with the existing single-flight safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
4. Tests updated: floor enforcement (values below floor rejected/clamped), cadence honored in the poll loop, idle-gate still requires the threshold to elapse, no dispatch while slots busy.
5. Measured outcome: mean inter-dispatch gap in the cheap window drops vs. baseline (146s/312s observed), and/or more sessions dispatched per night, without breaching proxy status-endpoint load limits.

## Notes

- Constants in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`: `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS = 10_000`, `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_FLOOR_MS = 1_000`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 60_000`.
- The 10s floor comment says "must not hammer the proxy" — quantify actual load before lowering; the status endpoint (`/llama/local/status`) is a cheap local JSON read, so the floor is expected to be safely reducible.
- Recommended: couple with the concurrent-dispatch item (bounded concurrency) so the faster cadence feeds more than one slot rather than just firing more single dispatches.
- Related: WL-0MSG80254005ZNE9 (proxy status poller), WL-0MSG80J5W007DVJ4 (timer loop), WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (idle tracker); evidence in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`.
data.title: Faster downtime dispatch cadence: reduce poll interval below 10s floor and lower idle threshold

## Problem statement

Two coupled defects leave valid audits visible as stale ("out of date audit"):

1. **Comment bumps invalidate audits.** `wl comment add` → `createComment` → `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (packages/shared/src/database.ts:3282, persistent-store `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` ~3416) advances the work item `updatedAt` for ANY comment. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (packages/shared/src/icons.ts:269) compares `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`; a comment added after the audit (e.g. "Audit re-evaluation (forced --force)" on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B at 21:26:17Z vs audit 21:21:03Z) therefore flips the audit to stale ⏳ even though no content changed. The documented guarantee in icons.ts ("Flag-only flips of needsProducerReview do not move updatedAt, so a previously valid audit remains fresh") does NOT cover comments — comments are the common case that breaks it.

2. **Audit persistence does not atomically update auditedAt.** `wl audit-set` (src/commands/audit-result.ts) writes the `audit_results` row (auditedAt = now) but does not touch the work item; `wl update --audit-text` (src/commands/update.ts) also only writes `saveAuditResult`. There is no single atomic operation that both records the audit AND refreshes the freshness clock, so a comment between audit and display (or a re-evaluation that comments instead of persisting — see WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF) leaves the record behind `updatedAt`.

Investigation outcome — audit-content comments can be removed (no consumer parses them):
- implement skill: reads the audit **record** (`/skill:audit` → runner → `wl audit-show`; `audit_report_<id>.md`); comments are only generic context in Step 4 ("pay attention to comments"), never parsed as verdicts
- ship skill `check-audit-gate.js`: `wl audit-show` → `readyToClose`/`rawOutput`/`summary`; `wl comment add` is used only to WRITE merge logs
- heartbeat, report skill, herdr TUI (`worklist.ts`, icons): all read `auditResult`/`auditedAt` from the record

So the audit verdict must live in the audit record only; audits duplicated in comments are dead weight and actively harmful (they bump updatedAt).

Discovered-from: WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B.

## Desired change

1. **Freshness clock:** make audit freshness reflect content-only changes. Options to evaluate (pick one, document trade-offs):
   a. exclude comments (and `needsProducerReview` flag flips, already excluded) from `updatedAt` bumps via `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt`; or
   b. `isAuditFresh` uses a content/activity fingerprint rather than `updatedAt`; or
   c. `wl audit-set`/`--audit-text` perform an atomic "record audit + set updatedAt = auditedAt" so a later comment still breaks it (not fully fixing) — likely insufficient alone.
2. **Atomic audit persistence:** `wl audit-set` (and/or `wl update --audit-text`) should be a single operation that records the `audit_results` row and refreshes the item's freshness marker so "audit recorded" always implies "audit fresh" immediately.
3. **Remove audit-content comments:** stop adding the audit report/verdict to work-item comments (the verdict lives in the audit record). Keep comments for dispatches/trails (herdr "Auto-dispatched…" is a dispatch marker, not audit content — out of scope) and for human annotations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a post-audit comment is added, the audit remains fresh: `wl show <id> --json` + a comment → `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` stays true; TUI keeps the passed icon, not ⏳ (add a regression test in packages/shared tests for the chosen mechanism)
- [ ] `wl audit-set` is atomic: after it, `auditedAt >= updatedAt` immediately (no intermediate window where a read shows stale) — or the alternative chosen mechanism guarantees the same
- [ ] The audit report/verdict is no longer duplicated into work-item comments by audit flows; existing duplicated comments on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B are documented as legacy (no migration required unless trivially safe)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: comment-after-audit keeps fresh; audit-then-comment ordering matches the chosen freshness clock; `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically to `wl audit-set`
- [ ] Docs updated: icons.ts guarantee comment, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md (or equivalent), audit SKILL.md where it describes the audit record as canonical
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh`, `stageDisplayIcon` (the ⏳ stale-passed path)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `createComment`/`touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (~3246, 3416)
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` — `wl audit-set` (atomic auditedAt write)
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--audit-text` persistence path
- `src/commands/comment.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — comment updatedAt semantics
- `packages/shared/src/icons.test.ts` (or equivalent) — freshness regression tests

## Related work

- WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B — observed stale audit (discovered-from)
- WL-0MT8KSTOE00871E7 — herdr interim freshness re-check (sibling)
- WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF — forced re-evaluation must persist (sibling; comment-only re-eval is the trigger that exposed this)
- WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R — flag-only flips do not move updatedAt (docs this gap for the needsProducerReview case)

# Indent group headings in children list

## Problem Statement

When expanding a parent item in the Herdr selection list extension, child work items are indented to reflect their hierarchy depth, but the **group heading rows** that separate groups within the children list are rendered at column 0. The headings should be indented to the same depth as the children they precede, so the hierarchy reads consistently.

## Users

- Herdr operators navigating hierarchical work items (parent → children at any depth) who see group headings visually "break out" of the child indentation.

### User Stories

- As a Herdr operator, I expand a parent item whose children are split into multiple groups, so that each group heading is indented at the same level as the child items beneath it, matching the hierarchy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Group heading rows that appear within an expanded parent's children (depth ≥ 1) are rendered with the same depth indentation as the child items they precede.
2. Top-level group headings (depth 0) are unchanged — no indentation added at the root list.
3. Heading depth derives from the same display-row model as item depth (the heading row carries the depth at which its group transition occurred), so nested children at depth 2+ indent correctly too.
4. Navigation, group collapse/expand, click-row mapping, and the `rows - 1` line-count invariant are unaffected by the change.
5. Unit tests cover: a group heading inside an expanded parent renders with indentation equal to its children's depth; a top-level heading renders unindented; nested (depth 2) headings render with two-level indentation.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Platform-independent rendering: changes stay within the display-rows model (`worklist.ts`); no Herdr socket API involvement.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** Heading indentation inside children subtrees should match the item indentation at the same depth (2 spaces per level), not a separate scheme.
- **Assumption (out of scope):** The heading `count` shown inside a children subtree is computed from top-level items of that group number (`groupCounts` from `this.items`), so it may not reflect the number of children shown beneath it. - **Scope-creep risk:** Rendering changes for headings inside children (colour, arrow, truncation) are out of scope — only indentation. Record any follow-ups as new work items.

- `WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()` inserts `DisplayHeadingRow` entries when the group changes between consecutive flattened items, including within expanded-parent subtrees. `DisplayHeadingRow` carries `kind`, `group`, `groupLabel`, `count`, `collapsed` — but **no depth**.

2. In `getDisplayRows().appendItem()`, stamp the current recursion `depth` onto newly inserted heading rows.
3. In `createListRenderer`, prepend `'  '.repeat(depth)` to the heading line when `depth > 0`.
4. Add/extend unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist-heading-rows.test.ts` and `worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts`.

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-heading-rows.test.ts` — display-rows model tests.

# Single machine-wide downtime leader across all worklogs (replace per-worklog elections)

## Problem statement

Leadership today is **per-worklog** (`coordinationDir: join(targetCwd, '.worklog')` in `index.ts`; per-entry `directory: coordinator.cwd` in `runCoordinationCheckIn`). Every open project tab therefore runs its own election, its own lease/lock, and its own coordination file. The parent refactor WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL and its docs page (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §Multi-worklog support) describe a leader that "compares offers across directories" — but no instance ever sees another worklog's offers, so that behaviour does not exist in practice. Consequences:

1. **N leaders, not 1** — TCE, ContextHub, and SorraAgents each have an independent leader (`22a6e7c7…`, `2a3f2a88…`, `97eb89d8…` observed), each polling the same shared llama-proxy.
2. **No cross-project slot budget** — all leaders see the same "3 free slots" in an idle window and can each dispatch within seconds of each other, oversubscribing the shared LLM (2-slot audit dispatches from two projects at once).
3. **Per-project ~1 item/hour cadence** — each project's leader runs the same single-entry→empty-file→no-candidate→1h-cooldown cycle (WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7), so total throughput across projects is low and uneven.
4. **Zombie leaders compound this** — expired leases never refresh (WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD); a machine-wide design with one lease per machine removes most of the multi-leader divergence surface.

## Goal

A single machine-wide downtime coordinator shared by every herdr instance on the host, regardless of which worklog its tab is open on: one coordination dir, one leader election, one lease, one dispatch queue containing per-worklog offers, and one slot budget against the shared proxy. This is the "multi-worklog leader" the architecture doc already implies.

## Proposed design

- **Machine-scoped coordination dir** — e.g. `~/.herdr/downtime/` (or `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` env override), containing `coordination.json`, `leader-lease.json`, `leader.lock`, `dispatches.log`. All instances read/write the same files regardless of project.
- **Per-worklog offers** — each instance contributes `{instanceId, workItemId, worklogRoot, assignedAt, lastUpdated}` (add `worklogRoot`; today's `directory` field is already the worklog root). Stale-entry pruning and 30-min check-in cadence carry over per instance.
- **One election, one lease** — instances elect a single machine leader (file lock + lease, reuse `leader-election.ts`); the lease must survive no-candidate cooldowns (depends on WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD fix).
- **Cross-directory dispatch** — the leader orders offers by the existing tier priority (audit → implement → plan → intake) *across* worklog roots, and spawns panes into each entry's `worklogRoot` (viaroot `wl` invocation as today).
- **Machine slot budget** — the leader enforces total concurrently-attributed panes/slots against the shared proxy status, so two projects cannot oversubscribe together. Coordinate with WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q (bounded concurrent dispatches within a project).
- **Migration/fallback** — while legacy per-worklog files still exist, prefer the machine dir; document how to retire the old `.worklog/downtime-*` files. Must not double-dispatch during the transition (a TCE instance with an old TCE file must not ALSO join the machine file with a different instanceId).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: One coordination dir shared by all instances on the host; a second instance opened on a *different* worklog joins the same file (contains entries with different `worklogRoot`s).
- [ ] AC2: Exactly one leader machine-wide: with N instances across P worklogs, only one holds a valid lease and no two instances dispatch in the same tick window (tested for the zombie case from WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD).
- [ ] AC3: Leader dispatches across directories by tier priority — e.g. a ContextHub audit offer is picked before a TCE intake offer, and the pane spawns in the ContextHub root.
- [ ] AC4: Global slot budget: with 3 proxy slots and 2 projects offering work, total concurrently dispatched/requesting work never exceeds the budget (no cross-project oversubscription).
- [ ] AC5: Migration is safe — existing per-worklog coordination files stop being written once the machine dir is authoritative; no double-dispatch during transition; docs (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) updated to match actual behaviour.
- [ ] AC6: Full herdr test suite + `npm run build` green; headless tests prove the AC1–AC4 invariants.

## Notes

- Builds on / must land after the two critical fixes: WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 (cooldown stall) and WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD (zombie lease).
- Supersedes the un-implemented "multi-worklog" paragraph of `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`; that doc must be corrected rather than describing aspirational behaviour.
- v1 remains single-machine; multi-machine (flock/NFS) stays out of scope.

`refreshLease()` currently guards `if (!this.isLeader()) return`; `isLeader()` requires `isLeaseValid` (>10 s remaining). An owned-but-EXPIRED lease therefore makes `refreshLease()` silently no-op forever — the zombie can never renew. Change the guard from 'valid leader' to 'owner of the lease': renew whenever `lease.leaderId === instanceId`, regardless of current validity.

- [ ] `refreshLease()` remains a no-op when the lease is owned by another instance (never renews/stops a foreign lease; takeover-race safe).
- [ ] `refreshLease()` remains a no-op when the lease file is missing or unreadable (fail-safe: not leader).

## Summary

In `tick()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`), `leaderState` is cached once at worker creation and only re-derived in an unreachable-while-leader takeover branch — an expired lease while `leaderState === true` leaves the worker dispatching as a zombie. Re-derive `leaderState` EVERY tick and add an explicit lease-renewal + re-derivation hook on cooldown exit (before any dispatch decision on resume).

CRITICAL interaction (found in plan review): `detectStaleLeader()` returns `false` for our OWN lease, so per-tick re-derivation alone would fall through BOTH the leader branch (leaderState=false) AND the takeover branch (hasLease=true, detectStaleLeader=false) — the self-heal (F4) would be starved. The leader branch must treat an owned-but-expired lease as refreshable, ensuring the self-heal is reachable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `leaderState` re-derived every tick (single cheap lease-file read) — a lease that expired mid-pause routes the worker OUT of zombie dispatch.
- [ ] Owned-but-expired lease in the leader block: `refreshLease()` (self-heal, F4) is invoked so the lease renews — never silently ignored.
- [ ] Cooldown-exit hook: when `cooldownUntil` expires, renew the lease (if leader) and re-derive leadership BEFORE any poll/dispatch decision — belt-and-braces even when the tick loop stalled mid-pause.
- [ ] Takeover-race guard: if ANOTHER instance won the lease during the pause, the re-derived state yields (worker stays silent) — never fights the new leader, never double-dispatch.
- [ ] Non-leader with a valid foreign lease stays silent (existing behavior preserved).
- [ ] Fail-safe preserved: missing/unreadable lease ⇒ treated as not leader.
- [ ] All existing unit + integration tests pass; F1/F2 regression tests (zombie, cooldown) pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace cached `let leaderState = ...` with per-tick `const leaderState = leaderManager ? leaderManager.isLeader() : true` (or re-derive at the top of the leader block each tick).
- In the leader block: `if (leaderState)` refresh OR `if (owned lease)` refresh-self-heal; keep takeover branch for foreign/stale/no-lease.
- In the cooldown-expiry branch (currently `cooldownUntil = null; errorStrikes = 0;`): before resuming, renew lease when owner, re-derive leadership, and if no longer leader stay silent this tick.

## Dependencies

- F1/F2 (red regression tests) and F4 (self-heal); green after this change.

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (tick() leader block + cooldown-exit hook).

# Intake Brief: Remove OpenBrain (WL-0MTH28WDS008WMXA)

## Problem statement

OpenBrain is an optional integration (`src/openbrain.ts`) that spawns the `ob` CLI to submit a summary whenever a work item is marked completed. This project enabled it for local testing (`openBrainEnabled: true` in `.worklog/config.yaml`, commit `66fb51a8`) but the `ob` binary is not installed, so every `wl update`/`wl close` that completes an item emits `[openbrain] ...` errors to stderr. The integration is unused and, per producer confirmation, is to be **removed entirely** — both from the shared codebase and from this project's config.

## Users

- **Developers** running `wl update`/`wl close` in this project — they see stray `[openbrain]` errors and want clean output.
- **Worklog maintainers** — they want dead integration code (which requires an `ob` binary nobody has and whose `wl openbrain` commands were never implemented) removed from the shared CLI.

User stories:
- As a developer in this project, I want `wl update` to complete a work item without emitting `[openbrain]` errors, so my terminal output is clean.
- As a Worklog maintainer, I want the OpenBrain integration absent from the shared codebase, so there is no dead code and no misleading docs/plugin references.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Feature removed from the shared codebase**: `src/openbrain.ts` deleted; `submitToOpenBrain` imports and call sites removed from `src/commands/update.ts` and `src/commands/close.ts`; `openBrainEnabled` removed from `WorklogConfig` in `packages/shared/src/types.ts`.
2. **Project-scoped disablement**: `openBrainEnabled: true` removed from `.worklog/config.yaml` in this repository.
3. **No dangling references or dead artifacts**: `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`, and `docs/openbrain.md` deleted; OpenBrain references removed from `CLI.md` and `README.md`. A repo-wide search (`rg -i "openbrain|submitToOpenBrain|openBrainEnabled"`) returns no matches in tracked source/docs (excluding git history and regenerated `dist/` artifacts).
4. **Error gone**: completing a work item via `wl update` and `wl close` in this project produces no `[openbrain]` stderr output (validated by the CLI test run, AC5).
5. **Green build & docs**: full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related documentation reflects the removal (README, CLI.md, code comments, docs table).

## Constraints

- No behavior changes beyond removing the OpenBrain path — `wl close`/`wl update` semantics (recursive close, re-sort, audit handling) are untouched.
- Worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/*` are separate feature branches — do not edit them in this change; only the main checkout is in scope.
- Config user file `.worklog/config.yaml` is the only place `openBrainEnabled` is set in this repo; `config.defaults.yaml` does not set it (verify at implementation time).
- The optional retry-queue file `.worklog/openbrain-queue.jsonl` may exist from failed submissions; it is transient data, not code — no action required beyond optionally removing it.

## Existing state

- `src/openbrain.ts` implements `submitToOpenBrain()` (spawns `ob add --stdin --title …`), `buildOpenBrainSummary()`, `appendToQueue()` (retry queue), and `resolveObBinary()` (`WL_OB_BIN` or `ob`).
- `src/commands/update.ts`: calls `submitToOpenBrain(item)` when `updates.status === 'completed'` and `config.openBrainEnabled`.
- `src/commands/close.ts`: calls `submitToOpenBrain(updated)` from the force, audit-gated recursive, and standard close paths when `config.openBrainEnabled`; the recovery path comments reference OpenBrain.
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: `WorklogConfig` declares `openBrainEnabled?: boolean`.
- `.worklog/config.yaml`: `openBrainEnabled: true`.
- Docs: `docs/openbrain.md`; `CLI.md` lists `wl openbrain status/resubmit` (commands were never implemented); `README.md` docs table links `docs/openbrain.md`.
- Tests: `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`.
- `ob` is not on PATH and `WL_OB_BIN` is unset; the globally installed `wl` (`/usr/local/bin/wl`) symlinks to this repo's built `dist/cli.js`, so a rebuild is required to actually stop the errors.

## Desired change

Remove the OpenBrain integration and its project config toggle:

- Delete `src/openbrain.ts`, `docs/openbrain.md`, `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts`, `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts`.
- In `src/commands/update.ts` / `src/commands/close.ts`: drop the `submitToOpenBrain` import and every `openBrainEnabled` fire-and-forget block (including the recovery-path comment).
- In `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: remove `openBrainEnabled?: boolean`.
- In `.worklog/config.yaml`: remove `openBrainEnabled: true`.
- In `CLI.md` / `README.md`: remove OpenBrain references.
- Rebuild (`npm run build:shared && npm run build`) so the installed `wl` no longer ships `openbrain.js` in `dist/`.

## Key Files:

- `src/openbrain.ts` — delete (entire module)
- `src/commands/update.ts` — remove import + completion call block
- `src/commands/close.ts` — remove import + three close-path call blocks + recovery comment
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — remove `openBrainEnabled` from `WorklogConfig`
- `.worklog/config.yaml` — remove `openBrainEnabled: true`
- `tests/unit/openbrain.test.ts` — delete
- `tests/cli/openbrain-close.test.ts` — delete
- `docs/openbrain.md` — delete
- `docs/feature-requests/openbrain-playwright-fallback-retrieval.md` — delete (OpenBrain feature request; would fail AC3 repo-wide search)
- `CLI.md`, `README.md` — remove OpenBrain references

## Related work

- WL-0MNM4SDMA000GOBC — "Whenever a work item is marked as completed/done update OpenBrain": introduced the integration (predecessor).
- WL-0MOHP1FIP007LYCB — "Make wl close OpenBrain submission fully non-blocking": changed the close flow (predecessor).
- WL-0MNRPS89H004COB0 — "Fix validator and openbrain test failures": fixed CLI.md docs + EPIPE handling (predecessor).
- WL-0MRTSOK8C009CDLA — "Process lifecycle utility module": references `src/openbrain.ts` as a spawn user; the process-lifecycle/spawn helpers themselves must be preserved.
- WL-0MQP4RDG2006LFM9 — ruff lint fix whose description matched `docs/openbrain.md` (search-index noise only).

## Effort and Risk

- Effort: **S** — deletions plus a handful of targeted edits; rebuild required.
- Risk: **Low** — opt-in flag; no other project enables it; `ob` unavailable so no live dependents. Residual risks: missed references (mitigated by the AC3 repo-wide search) and stale built `dist/` (mitigated by the rebuild in Desired change / AC5).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** (Map/intake, 2026-09-19): "Should 'Remove openbrain' mean (A) remove the integration from the shared `worklog` codebase (~600 lines), or (B) only disable it in this project's `.worklog/config.yaml` (one line)? The title points at (A), the description ('in this project, but not any other … disable it') at (B). Reply A, B, or both."

# Dispatch-logs Skill: Generate Global Dispatch Reports

A `/skill:dispatch-logs` command that produces a concise, human-readable (or JSON) 24-hour dispatch activity report across all projects on the machine — including leader state, timeline, errors, and coordination status — with support for custom time windows and per-project filtering.

## Problem Statement

Operators investigating overnight dispatches must manually aggregate `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` files across all projects on the machine. There is no single command to produce a concise 24-hour (or custom window) global dispatch report.

## Users

- **Operator on-call**: Needs a quick view of what dispatches ran overnight and whether any errors occurred.
- **Debugging engineer**: Tracing a specific dispatch failure across projects.
- **Team lead**: Reviewing dispatch activity trends over a custom time window.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:dispatch-logs` produces a human-readable report covering all projects on the machine for the last 24 hours (default window).
2. All invocation flags work correctly: `--hours N`, `--since`/`--until` ISO timestamps, `--project <name>`, and `--json` for machine-readable output.
3. The report includes five sections: (a) leader summary, (b) dispatch timeline, (c) error summary, (d) coordination state, and (e) known issues.
4. Gracefully handles the case when no dispatch logs exist (produces an empty/clean report, not an error).
5. Unit tests pass for log parsing, argument handling, and report structure (using mocked log files).
6. SKILL.md is complete with name, description, invocation examples, and frontmatter.

## Constraints

- Log files are in JSONL format (one JSON object per line).
- Machine coordination state lives in `~/.herdr/downtime/` (two JSON files).
- Must skip `node_modules`, `dist`, `build` directories during project root discovery.
- Default window is 24 hours from `Date.now()`; custom windows use ISO 8601 timestamps.

## Existing State

- Per-worklog dispatch logs exist at `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- Machine-wide coordination at `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` and `downtime-leader-lease.json`.
- Companion debug item (WL-0MTJPYM53003ORCV) adds per-strike stderr/exitCode — the dispatch-logs skill should note when this data is unavailable.

## Desired Change

Create a new skill in `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/` with:
- `SKILL.md` — skill definition with frontmatter and invocation docs.
- `scripts/dispatch-logs.py` — Python script implementing the report generation.
- `tests/dispatch-logs.test.py` — unit tests with mocked data.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/SKILL.md` — New skill definition file.
- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/scripts/dispatch-logs.py` — Core logic: argument parsing, log discovery, parsing, report generation.
- `.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/tests/dispatch-logs.test.py` — Unit tests.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` — Read-only coordination state.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-leader-lease.json` — Read-only leader lease.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: Resist adding extra report sections beyond the five specified (leader summary, dispatch timeline, error summary, coordination state, known issues).
- **Discovery performance**: Walking from `~` to find all project roots could be slow on machines with many repositories; consider caching or a configurable root list.
- **JSONL format consistency**: Assumes all projects write logs in the same JSONL format; malformed lines should be skipped gracefully.
- **Coordination files**: Assumes `~/.herdr/downtime/` files are present and readable; handle missing files gracefully.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MTJPYM53003ORCV** — "Downtime dispatcher: make wl-error pauses debuggable" (companion; provides richer per-strike data the dispatch-logs skill should report on).
- **WL-0MU4URK4H006OFCE** — "Extend dispatch log schema and add pane lifecycle monitor" (may affect log parsing).
- **WL-0MU8808ZY0091JIA** — "Downtime dispatcher: log the actual no-dispatch reason" (enriches available log data).
- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — "Log herdr downtime dispatches" (established the per-worklog log architecture).
