# Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`) and the Herdr extension selection list (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` → `worklist.ts`) disagree on "most important item" because the dispatcher maintains its own tier ordering (`wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` audit query) instead of reusing the Herdr list. The project needs the dispatcher to consume the Herdr list head so the two selectors agree by construction. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`" scope per producer determination WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 (2026-09-02).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy queue; the item dispatched during downtime was visible at the top of `prefix+l` and reflects declared prioritization intent.
- **Herdr user browsing `prefix+l`** — expects downtime work to track exactly what the visible list shows, so automated work does not appear arbitrary.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl next** — needs a single ranking contract; ranking logic lives only in the fetcher/smart-selection/grouping/database pipeline.

Example user stories:
- As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher to pick the first item shown in the Herdr list, so automated work follows the priority I already see.
- As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been at the head of the Herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen.
- As a maintainer, I want the ranking contract documented as "dispatcher == Herdr list head" so future safety gates are evaluated as filters, not a competing ranking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head** — `dispatchDowntimeWork` (and any coordination-leader path) derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head rather than a separate tier ordering / stage-scoped `wl next` / `wl list` audit query. No second ranking implementation remains on the dispatch path.
2. **No duplicate ranking; gates are filters** — tier ordering / `wl next --stage` per-tier calls / audit `wl list` ranking are no longer used to pick "most important". Any safety gates that must remain (code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight / CAS claim) act as sequential filters on the Herdr-ordered candidates. If no Herdr-ordered candidate passes the filters, the dispatcher reports "no candidate" rather than falling back to a separate ranking.
3. **Herdr list remains sole ranking path** — `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` stay the sole ranking path (mandatory-always for critical + `completed`/`in_review`, `browseItemCount` windowing of "other" items, grouping logic, `reSort`/`computeScore` as used by the fetcher). No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change is required to fix the divergence; if `fetchNextItems` delegates to `wl next` internally that internal detail is acceptable — the observable contract is "dispatcher == Herdr list head".
4. **Contract documented** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` (and `src/commands/next.ts` help if it references dispatcher selection) state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list; any remaining safety override (e.g. code-freeze) is documented as a skip/filter on that sequence, not a ranking.
5. **No regression; observable agreement proven** — existing `wl next` / herdr fetcher/grouping / downtime-worker fixtures pass; a reproducible sampling script shows `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree (downtime picks the list head after filtering) on a fixture. Dispatched-marker / code-freeze / single-flight gating still respected as filters on the Herdr sequence.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr; `smart-selection.ts`/`grouping.ts` duplicated per TUI stays in sync with `src/commands/*` if touched.
- `browseItemCount` clamping (1–50) and root-only / `done`-exclusion rules respected.
- Do not fork a second ranking; reuse the Herdr list pipeline.
- Investigation only touched the prior item (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q); this item carries the implementation.
- Backwards compat: existing dispatched-marker / code-freeze gating semantics preserved as filters.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets via `fetchMandatorySubsets` (`wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`), applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review). Rendered via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order audit → implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete` with risk/effort caps) → plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`) → fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` with 7-day recency / dispatched-marker / active-audit / code-freeze gates; pre-dispatch CAS claim, per-process single-flight, scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin cursor, cooldowns.
- **Shared scoring:** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (`computeScore`/`reSort`/`filterCandidates`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`) and `src/commands/next.ts` auto `reSort` — shared by `wl next` but not required to change for this contract; the observable contract is Herdr list head.
- All divergence gaps mapped in WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q (cap 32 / mandatory merge / stage-scoped calls / audit `wl list` source / tier order / risk-effort gates / code-freeze tri-state, etc.) — eliminated by consuming the Herdr order directly.

## Desired change

Replace the dispatcher's independent tier ordering with consumption of the Herdr selection list head:

- Refactor `downtime-worker.ts` to invoke (or share code with) the Herdr fetcher/selection pipeline to obtain the ordered candidate sequence, then apply only the necessary safety filters (code-freeze, dispatched-marker, single-flight/active-audit) sequentially on that sequence.
- Remove or dead-code the tier-ordering / per-stage `wl next` / audit `wl list` ranking path from the dispatch decision (or leave only as unused fallback behind a feature flag with a clear deprecation note).
- Document the contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head; filters, not ranking") in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Herdr selection pipeline reused by dispatcher
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — mandatory-always + browseItemCount logic
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — regroupWorkItems / assignItemGroups ordering
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — rendering consuming grouped selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatchDowntimeWork to be refactored to consume list head (+ fixtures)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — computeScore/reSort/filterCandidates as used by fetcher (not dispatcher ranking)
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/grouping.ts` — wl next entry point as used by fetcher
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher contract doc
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr list contract doc

## Related work

- Investigation: WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q — downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list divergence (producer determination revised 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, superseding WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS) → follow-up direction is this item.
- WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX — counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (symptom of cap/mandatory interaction; not blocking but shares fetcher context)
- WL-0MS8XL3EW006Y04G / WL-0MSKCRX730052iiw / WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR — Herdr smart selection / in_review / root-only rules shaping mandatory set
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 / WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG — implement tier + risk/effort filters wired into wl next / dispatcher (removed or converted to filters in this work)
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN / WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatched-marker exclusion, conditional claim, dispatch logging (preserved as filters)
- WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6 — priority-first with round-robin tie-break (cursor handling to reconcile with Herdr order)
- RCA docs: `downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`, `downtime-disable-incident-rca-2026-08-22.md` — prior tier/re-dispatch incidents

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "selection list" means herdr `prefix+l` Work Items list (`fetchNextItems` path); "downtime dispatcher" means `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier loop in `downtime-worker.ts` (including coordination leader path if any).
- Assumption: producer wants a single notion of "most important" — confirmed 2026-09-02 (Herdr list canonical; dispatcher consumes head).
- Risk: code-freeze / audit safety behavior at head — if the list head must be skipped, the skip order must be explicit and remain a filter on the Herdr sequence; document clearly.
- Risk: `in_review` mandatory-always items in the list — dispatcher taking the head must still respect `completed`/`in_review` dispatchability; filter vs ranking distinction must be explicit to avoid re-dispatching audits.
- Risk: spare-capacity / idle-budget / round-robin cursor logic must be reconciled as filters or removed; otherwise a second ordering re-emerges.
- Scope-creep risk: unifying ranking touches herdr selection and downtime-worker — keep scope to dispatcher-consumes-head; do not rework scoring or grouping unless required for the contract. Extra opportunities → new work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'most important,' do you mean the Herdr list order or the dispatcher tier order?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, rescoping WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2; supersedes WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS): **Herdr extension selection list order is authoritative** (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). Dispatcher selects the first item in that list — no second ranking. Source: producer comment WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.
- Q2: "Should the two selectors be unified to one shared ranking, or should the dispatcher intentionally differ (e.g. audit-first)?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **Unified on the Herdr list** — single source of truth; dispatcher consumes the list head. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`". Source: same producer determination.
- Q3: "For sampling, which `browseItemCount` / `wl next -n` window and which worklog root should be the reference?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS as affirmed by WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **LGTM** — default `browseItemCount` / ContextHub root / `wl next -n 20` accepted as sampling reference. Source: producer comment on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.

No open questions. Interview skipped — seed context and revised producer determination (WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1) already provide a clear, testable brief.

# Intake Brief — Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace (route each prefix to its own tab) (WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC)

**Headline**: Extend the now-correct Dispatcher-workspace anchor so every automated downtime dispatch lands in a per-project tab inside the Dispatcher workspace, named after the work-item prefix (e.g. `WL`, `TCE`), giving operators instant per-project separation without leaving the neutral workspace.

## Problem statement

The automated downtime dispatcher has been fixed to always spawn into a dedicated **Dispatcher** workspace regardless of which herdr instance holds the leader lease (WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG / WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX, F1–F3 landed on `origin/dev`). All dispatches currently share the single root tab/pane in that workspace. With two active worklogs (ContextHub `WL-…`, Tableau Card Engine `CG-/TCE-…`, plus other roots) this collapses per-project separation — overnight runs for different projects intermix in one grid and operators must inspect each pane's `cwd`/label to tell them apart.

## Users

- **Herdr operator running 2+ project workspaces** (e.g. ContextHub, Podcast-editor, Tableau Card Engine):
  > "As an operator, I want every automated downtime pane that belongs to project prefix `TCE` to appear in a `TCE` tab of the Dispatcher workspace (and `WL` panes in a `WL` tab), so I can see per-project progress at a glance without mixing projects in one grid."

- **On-call / overnight dispatch reviewer**:
  > "As an on-call engineer reviewing morning dispatches, I want the Dispatcher workspace to contain one tab per project (labelled by the work-item prefix), so I can sweep each project's automated work independently."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-prefix tab routing inside the Dispatcher workspace** — an automated downtime dispatch for work item `<PREFIX>-<hash>` creates (if absent) or reuses a tab labelled `<PREFIX>` inside the machine-wide Dispatcher workspace and spawns its pane inside that tab. Example: `WL-0MTO…` → `WL` tab, `TCE-…` / `CG-…` → tab named exactly after the id prefix before `-` (so `TCE` items land in `TCE`, `WL` items in `WL`). Verified via `herdr tab list` (tabs filtered to `workspace_id == Dispatcher` carry `label == prefix`) and `herdr pane list` (each `Downtime triggered …` pane's `workspace_id == Dispatcher` and `tab_id` equals the prefix tab's `tab_id`, with `cwd` equal to the item's worklog root).
2. **Idempotent, concurrent-safe tab provisioning** — the first dispatch for a previously unseen prefix creates the tab exactly once; concurrent first-dispatches for the same new prefix do not create duplicate tabs with the same label in the Dispatcher workspace. Re-provisioning handles stale state: a persisted per-prefix anchor whose tab/pane is no longer alive is detected and re-created on the next dispatch for that prefix.
3. **No regression to existing dispatcher invariants** — Dispatcher-workspace anchoring (no fallback to the leader's current pane — `anchor-unavailable` still means "no dispatch this cycle"), per-item `cwd` forwarding, CAS `wl update --if-status/--if-stage` claim, staged-marker exclusion, `code-freeze` and `needsProducerReview` gates, selection/coordination/round-robin semantics, and dispatch audit logs (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`) remain unchanged; pane spawn still goes through `send-to-pi.sh` / `grid.py` (now targeting the per-prefix tab's anchor pane rather than the single workspace anchor when a prefix tab exists).
4. **No leftover duplicate workspace or orphan tab state** — after the change there remains exactly one `Dispatcher` workspace (label `Dispatcher`, `w13` today) holding all per-prefix tabs; repeated dispatches for the same prefix do not leak extra tabs or panes beyond the expected grid growth; a persisted file (e.g. extended `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` or a new `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` in the machine coordination dir) tracks `{ workspaceId, byPrefix: { "<PREFIX>": { tabId, paneId } } }` under the coordination lock and is the authority for reuse.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Automated downtime dispatch only — scope is `dispatchFromCoordination` / `dispatchDowntimeWork` → `dispatchClaimedTier`; manual `open-worklist` / `open-pi-agent` flows keep their current-pane/tab behavior.
- Single `Dispatcher` workspace (C0) is retained — per-project separation is by **tabs** inside it, not by additional workspaces.
- Prefix extraction is the work-item id substring before the first `-` (e.g. `WL-…` → `WL`, `TCE-…` → `TCE`, `CG-…` → `CG`); tab label is exactly that prefix (case-preserved, no normalisation beyond the raw prefix).
- Tab/pane provisioning must use the existing machine coordination dir (`~/.herdr/downtime`, via `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts`) and the coordination lock (`tryAcquireCoordLock`) — no new lock mechanism; `herdr tab create --workspace <id> --label <PREFIX> --no-focus` (or `workspace create` + `tab create`) and `herdr pane split --pane <anchorPaneId>` / `grid.py` remain the herdr surface.
- Fail-safe: if the per-prefix tab/anchor cannot be resolved/provisioned, the dispatch degrades to `anchor-unavailable` (no dispatch this cycle), never to a leader-workspace fallback or to the wrong tab.
- Herdr CLI JSON shapes may vary across versions (`tab_id` vs `tabId`, `pane_id` vs `paneId`, nested `result`) — parsers must tolerate variants and log raw output on parse failure rather than silently producing `anchor-unavailable` every cycle.

## Existing state

- **C0 anchor-by-ID landed on `origin/dev` (WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG):** `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` provisions one `Dispatcher` workspace + root pane and persists `{ paneId, workspaceId }` to `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` under the coordination lock with an aliveness (`pane get`) check and stale re-provision; `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchClaimedTier` resolves `getDispatcherAnchor(cwd)` before the CAS claim and forwards `anchorId` to `spawnAgentPane` → `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>` → `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py --cwd <target>` (split + rebalance around the anchor) or plain `pane split --pane <id>`.

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) runs `UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` (unless `--no-re-sort`), on create/update, so routine queue reads rewrite `updatedAt` on dozens of items at once (observed: 13 items at `2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z`, 88 items at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`).

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit. Concrete victim: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V audited "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03 now carries `updatedAt` 2026-09-11, so its passing audit reads stale and the item lingers in the open queue. Recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`) is also polluted.

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** a "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical re-sorts.
- **Heartbeat/audit pipeline:** must not re-audit items whose only change is sortIndex.

# Intake Brief — Smart Audit Re-instatement

**Headline:** When the audit freshness check (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) flags an audit as stale, the system should automatically review the changes made since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or flag the item for re-audit — rather than treating all post-audit changes as requiring a full re-run.

## Problem statement

Audits are invalidated whenever a work item's `updatedAt` changes after the audit time (`isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`). However, many changes do not affect the code or implementation that was audited (e.g., changing a comment, updating assignee). The audit skill should automatically inspect the changes since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or require a new one.

**Producer clarification:** The system should inspect anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it — description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI:** Audited items should not be unnecessarily re-audited when changes are irrelevant to the implementation.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited and whose changes are non-semantic.
- **Producers:** A "Ready to close: Yes" item should stay ready unless changes actually affect the audit outcome.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automatic re-instatement detection:** When `isAuditNotReadyFresh` returns `false` (audit flagged as stale), the system automatically inspects the changes made since `auditedAt` and decides whether to re-instate the audit or flag for re-audit.
2. **Change inspection covers key fields:** The inspection examines description, comments, audit text, dependencies, and commit messages for changes that could affect the audit outcome. Non-semantic changes (e.g., metadata-only updates) do not trigger re-audit.
3. **Re-instatement logic:** If changes are deemed non-semantic (no impact on audit outcome), the original audit is re-instated by resetting `updatedAt` to `auditedAt` (same pattern as `saveAuditResult`). If changes are semantic, the audit is flagged as needing re-run.
4. **Full project test suite passes** with new regression tests covering re-instatement of non-semantic changes and re-audit flag for semantic changes.

## Constraints

- Change confined to audit freshness logic in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and the audit result management in the persistent store.
- No schema changes required.
- Must preserve existing audit behavior for items with no previous audit.
- Must be fully automatic — no operator intervention required.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:644`** — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`. If false, the audit is treated as stale.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:1038`** — `saveAuditResult` resets `updatedAt = auditedAt` to keep audits fresh after audit writes.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`** — Audit results stored in SQLite; `getAllAuditResults` / `saveAuditResult` methods.

## Desired change

1. Create a new function `assessAuditInvalidate(changesSinceAudited, auditResult)` that inspects the delta between the audit time and current state.
2. The function should classify changes as semantic (affect audit outcome) or non-semantic (no impact).
3. For non-semantic changes, re-instate the audit (reset `updatedAt = auditedAt`).
4. For semantic changes, mark the audit as needing re-run.
5. Integrate into the `wl next` / TUI flow where audit freshness is checked.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` (line 644), audit map builder, sorting logic
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — Audit storage methods, `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line 747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` — Sync merge logic
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — Audit command integration point
- `src/pi-audit.ts` — Pi audit module

## Related work

- **WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO** — Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations (complementary; prevents timestamp churn, this handles post-invalidation review)
- **WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA** — Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn (child of WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO)
- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — Established the audit freshness rule (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Semantic boundary ambiguity:** What counts as a semantic change is subjective. **Assumption:** Changes to description, comments, dependencies, and commit messages are semantic; changes to assignee, tags, priority, and sortIndex are non-semantic. Document the rule in code comments.
- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable invalidation policies. **Mitigation:** Keep this to the concrete scenarios identified; file separate items for broader policy changes.
- **Performance risk:** Inspecting changes since audit could add overhead. **Mitigation:** Only run when freshness check fails; use efficient diff comparison.
- **Backward compatibility:** Existing audit behavior must be preserved for items with no previous audit result.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What specific change types should the audit skill inspect when deciding whether to re-instate an audit? — A: Anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it. So description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages etc. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: Should this be automatic (triggered when an invalidated audit is discovered) or manual (operator/producer-initiated)? — A: Automatic. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: How does this relate to WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO (Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations)? — A: Complementary — WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO prevents timestamp churn from invalidating audits, this item handles post-invalidation review to determine whether to re-instate or re-run. Source: interactive reply (producer).

# Herdr dispatcher ignores `needsProducerReview` on the live dispatch path

<<discovered-from>>:WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5

## Problem

`dispatchFromHerdrList` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) builds the
`DowntimeItemInfo` passed to `classifyItemForDispatch` from the Herdr head item
but OMITS `needsProducerReview`. `classifyItemForDispatch` blocks an item when
`info.needsProducerReview === true`, so on the live Herdr-head dispatch path the
flag is silently ignored and a `needsProducerReview: true` item dispatches anyway.

Reproduced while implementing WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5: `dispatchDowntimeWork` with a
Herdr head item `{ status:'open', stage:'plan_complete', priority:'critical',
risk:'Low', effort:'S', needsProducerReview:true }` dispatches it as
`/skill:implement` — the flag never reaches `classifyItemForDispatch`.

The offer path (`computeMostImportantItem`) passes the item object DIRECTLY to
`classifyItemForDispatch`, so the flag IS honoured there. The two paths disagree,
so the live dispatch path can auto-dispatch items the producer has explicitly
flagged for review.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `dispatchFromHerdrList` threads `needsProducerReview` into the
   `classifyItemForDispatch` input, so `needsProducerReview === true` items are
   never dispatched on the live Herdr-head path.
2. A regression test proves the flag blocks a `plan_complete`/idea/intake
   candidate on `dispatchDowntimeWork` (currently it does not).
3. The direct and offer paths agree on the producer-review gate.
4. `npm run build` and the suites pass.

## Constraints

- No second ranking: the fix is a field-threading correction on the existing
  sequential filter, not a new ordering.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: N/A — auto-plan (effort/risk below threshold, no decomposition needed).
  The item is a focused bug fix with clear ACs. Code fix was already applied in
  commit 022f1b24 (WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT). Remaining gap: AC2 regression test

# RCA: downtime dispatcher sends nothing in cheap mode despite 2–3 idle slots

## Symptom

In cheap mode the local llama-proxy reports 3 slots with 2–3 idle for extended periods, yet the
herdr downtime dispatcher produces no dispatches. Observed in the window immediately before the
proxy was switched to fast mode (2026-09-19 ~00:13Z).

## Evidence (llama-proxy status log, proxy clock = UTC+1)

Source: `GET http://192.168.0.199:8000/logs/tail?source=proxy&lines=100000` (log file starts at
proxy 00:00 = UTC 23:00 on 2026-09-18).

- Window proxy 01:01–01:12 = **UTC 00:01–00:12**: `mode=cheap`, `total_slots=3`,
  `available_slots=2` (constant — 2 slots idle), and **zero** dispatches in
  `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- `local_owner_session_id = ["http://localhost:8080","herdr-1789775322-722064-10708"]` — the owner
  is a **dispatched downtime pane** (`Downtime triggered implement … CG-0MTIOLY2A0092OT1`), whose
  local dispatch lease ran 836s → 0 across the window (`local_active_query=true` throughout).
- Across the whole UTC 23:00–04:11 log: **56%** of status samples had ≥2 idle slots **and** an
  active lease; **10%** had all slots idle **and** an active lease.

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()`:

```ts
const ownerLeaseHeld = /* local_owner_session_id string OR local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds > 0 */;
const slotOwned = ownerLeaseHeld && (runningPanes ?? 0) > 0;
const contentionQueueDepth = ...;
if (slotOwned) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
if (contentionQueueDepth > 0) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
```

This gate runs **before** the coordination file is read, is **machine-wide**, and has **no per-slot
branch** — it fires even in per-slot mode (`requiredFreeSlots=1 < total=3`). While any dispatched
agent is alive and holds the shared local-dispatch lease, the dispatcher refuses to dispatch at
all, leaving the remaining unowned free slots unused. In cheap mode a single long-running agent
therefore monopolises the dispatcher's permission for the whole generation (adaptive lease up to
`local_dispatch_lease_max_seconds`, default 1500s; observed 840s).

The code comment claims the gate is only a single-slot (count-based) fallback superseded by per-slot
identity, and that leases expire in ~180s. Both assumptions are false for this deployment.

## Contributing causes

1. **Owner-signal schema drift** — the proxy serves `local_owner_session_id` as a JSON **array**;
   `parseLlamaStatus` expects a **string** and silently drops it, so the worker cannot identify the
   owning slot/session and falls back to `lease_remaining > 0`.
2. **No queue-depth signal** — `contention_queue_depth` is not served in this configuration.
3. **Header vs proxy UI disagree** — the herdr header only shows idle when *all* slots are idle,
   while the proxy UI shows `available_slots`; "idle slots but no dispatches" is invisible in herdr.
4. **Scheduler targets the affected window** — the mode scheduler is `[('01:00','cheap'),('10:00','fast')]`,
   so the overnight window is precisely the one this gate wastes.

## Goal

Restore cheap-mode overnight throughput by removing the machine-wide dispatch block, aligning the
owner-lease contract, and making the gate decision observable.

## Acceptance criteria

1. In cheap mode with ≥1 unowned free slot, a dispatched agent holding a lease no longer prevents
   dispatch (measured: dispatches resume during agent runs).
2. The proxy owner-lease payload is parsed without silent data loss and covered by a contract test.
3. The dispatcher records *why* it did not dispatch (`slotOwned` / `contention` / `no-candidate` /
   `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze`) to `downtime-coordination.log` and the header.
4. The lease-TTL assumption in `downtime-worker.ts` matches the proxy's adaptive-lease behaviour.

Children cover each fix; see the child items of this RCA.

# Intake Brief: Client retry does not honor Retry-After (503 startup_ramp)

## Problem statement

The llm-proxy's **post-restart startup ramp** gate returns HTTP `503` with a
randomized `Retry-After` header (5-18 s) and a machine-readable body
(`{"error":{"type":"startup_ramp","code":"startup_ramp","message":"Server is starting up; retry shortly."},"status":503,"retry_after":N}`)
specifically so that clients spread their reconnects across the ramp window
(`startup_ramp.max_seconds: 180` in `proxy/config.yaml`; proxy side tracked as
LP-0MUA6RAMP001XXXX).

The Pi client does **not** honor that hint. Its *agent-level* auto-retry
(`getRetrySettings()` -> `retryDelayMs() = baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)`,
`baseDelayMs` default 2000 ms, cap 60 000 ms, **no jitter**) ignores both the
`Retry-After` header and the `retry_after` body field.

### Evidence (2026-09-20)

Proxy restarted at 16:11:28 local; the 180 s startup ramp was active until
~16:14:28. Session `herdr-1789917126-2590234-11663` (model `plan`, provider
`Local Proxy`), every turn failing with
`503: {"type":"startup_ramp",...}`:

| attempt | time (local) | gap vs prev |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| 1       | 16:12:10.5   | -           |
| 2       | 16:12:12.6   | +2.0 s      |
| 3       | 16:12:16.6   | +4.0 s      |
| 4       | 16:12:24.6   | +8.0 s      |
| 5       | 16:12:40.7   | +16.0 s     |
| 6       | 16:13:12.8   | +32.1 s     |
| 7       | 16:14:13.1   | +60.3 s     |

This is exactly `2000 * 2^(attempt-1)` capped at 60 000 ms - the client's own
deterministic backoff, independent of the `Retry-After` values the proxy
returned (random randint in [5,15] + 3 s margin per request, logged by the
proxy as `Startup ramp: deferring chat request (... retry_after=Ns)`).

A second session (`herdr-1789917234-2590706-9592`, this very analysis session)
shows the same `+2.0 / +4.0 / +8.0` pattern.

## Impact

1. Clients retry **sooner than instructed** (e.g. `Retry-After: 7` -> retry at
   2 s), hammering the freshly restarted proxy - the opposite of the ramp's
   intent.
2. Backoff has **no jitter**, so clients that started together retry in
   lockstep, defeating the ramp's desynchronisation goal.
3. The retry cap (`maxAgentDelayMs` 60 s) is shorter than the ramp window (up
   to 180 s), so a client can exhaust its retry budget mid-ramp and surface a
   hard failure to the user even though the server said "retry shortly".

## Users

- Operators/developers running herdr workers (Pi agents) against the local
  llm-proxy.
- Anyone whose first provider request after a mode switch / proxy restart lands
  inside the ramp window.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1**: When an OpenAI-compatible provider response carries `Retry-After`
  (delta-seconds or HTTP-date) and the request is retried, the client's delay is
  at least the server-requested delay (bounded by a configurable maximum,
  default 60 s).
- **AC2**: The `503 startup_ramp` body's `retry_after` field is honored as a
  fallback when the header is absent or unparseable.
- **AC3**: Missing/malformed hints fall back to the existing exponential
  backoff, unchanged.
- **AC4**: A client can survive a full startup ramp (up to
  `startup_ramp.max_seconds`, default 180 s) without exhausting its retry budget,
  or the ramp window is otherwise communicated so a long ramp does not surface
  as a final user-visible failure solely because the retry budget ran out first.
- **AC5**: Jitter is applied to (or combined with) any delay derived from the
  server hint so concurrent clients do not retry in lockstep.
- **AC6**: Tests cover header/body parsing, the cap, malformed values, and the
  long-ramp case; full suite green.
- **AC7**: No double-retry amplification between the provider-level and
  agent-level retry layers.

## Constraints

- Tracked in ContextHub; the change belongs in the **Pi coding agent codebase**
  (same arrangement as WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO).
- Pi already exposes a provider-level helper that *does* honor
  `retry-after`/`retry-after-ms` (`@earendil-works/pi-ai` -> `retryProviderRequest`),
  but it is effectively disabled: `openai-completions` calls it with
  `maxRetries` from `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, which is unset
  (-> 0). The active layer is the agent-level retry in `settings-manager` /
  `agent-session` / `retry.ts`, which ignores the hint. Reuse/extend the
  existing helper rather than adding a third retry path.
- Keep the change minimal; do not regress the completed
  WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO tuning. Note: the installed build observed here still
  shows `baseDelayMs = 2000` (not 7000), so verify version drift before
  assuming that tuning is present.

## Related work

- WL-0MPWVLT6Q0064MUO (completed) - "When a model is loading wait longer before
  retrying" (increased agent retry delays; did **not** add Retry-After honoring).
- llm-proxy startup ramp: LP-0MUA6RAMP001XXXX (proxy side, `/home/rgardler/projects/llm`).
- llm-proxy `Retry-After` emission: LP-0MPQ2PLTC000GYRZ, LP-0MQS6MPK9000UIZK.

## Out of scope

- The proxy-side startup-ramp behaviour itself (tracked in the llm project).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSWFQU9N002TAOA** – Implement post-persist lifecycle verification with retry (completed)
- **WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J** – Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (completed)
- **WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG** – Same-slot idle tracking for herdr downtime worker (per slot_id) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+166 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac5 (+131 more)

## Summary

Make child-audit coverage explicit so a child covered by a parent audit is not
treated as "no audit" by the icon and the downtime dispatcher.

## Problem

11 of the 12 `completed`/`in_review` items with **no** audit record are children
(e.g. `WL-0MTQ48YKS000PA6H`, `WL-0MU2LF6SZ000JQYI`, `WL-0MU2LFC1Y0077U1U`,
`WL-0MU2LFHBH004VF48`, `WL-0MUAG2S77003JGDL`, `WL-0MTF5WNRB009RHRU`). A parent audit
covers them (child verdicts are reused), but there is no record on the child itself.

- `stageDisplayIcon` falls back to the plain stage icon (no ✅/⏳), so the queue looks

- `selectAuditCandidate` filters `!isAuditFresh(c.auditedAt, c.updatedAt)`; a child

  re-dispatches a redundant child audit — which writes and creates more churn.

- A child covered by a parent audit is recorded as covered (inherited/parent audit
  reference or equivalent), and is not re-dispatched or shown as unaudited.
- A child genuinely not covered by any audit is still surfaced for audit.

1. Policy decided and documented: either (a) every child gets its own verdict, or
   (b) a child may record an inherited audit reference to its covering parent audit.

   reference; `isAuditFresh` (or its caller) treats a covered child as fresh.

# Downtime dispatcher stalls when llama-proxy serves slots:[] + slots_stale:true

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28. Discovered while verifying the parent's AC1 against the LIVE proxy during implementation of the four children.

## Evidence (live proxy, 2026-09-24)

`GET http://192.168.0.199:8000/llama/local/status`:

```json
{"active_query":true,"local_active_query":true,"model_switch_in_progress":false,"current_model":"Qwen3","llama_server_running":true,"available_slots":1,"total_slots":3,"slots_stale":true,"slots":[],"local_owner_session_id":["http://localhost:8080","herdr-1790261458-1799601-10619"],"local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds":645.5}
```

## Root cause

`parseLlamaStatus` accepts `slots: []` as a valid empty array and ignores the `slots_stale` field entirely. In `tick()`:

- `perSlotMode = Array.isArray(status.slots) && 0 < requiredFreeSlots < total_slots` -> **true** for `slots: []` (an empty array is still an array).
- `perSlotTracker.record([])` starts no timers -> `thresholdMetCount === 0 < requiredFreeSlots` -> `ready === false` -> tick returns `!ready` (idle, no dispatch).
- Even if `ready` were true, `slotOwned = countFreeUnownedSlots([]) === 0` -> true -> refusal.
- `freeSlots = countFreeUnownedSlots([]) = 0`.

When `slots` is absent (not `[]`), the count-based fallback is also blocked: the derived `local_lease_active` is true (owner array + 645 s lease), so `globalIdleChecks` fails.

Result: with `slots: []` / `slots_stale: true` and an active lease, the dispatcher NEVER dispatches — the RCA stall persists despite the child-1 per-slot fix (WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME).

## Proposed fix areas (to be planned)

1. Treat `slots_stale: true` (and/or an empty `slots` array) as "no per-slot identity": parse the flag and fall back to the count-based path.
2. In the count-based path, do not let a lease block dispatch when `available_slots >= requiredFreeSlots` and `total_slots > 1` (spare capacity) — only a truly owned SOLE slot should block.
3. Add a regression test pinned to the exact live payload above.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A payload with `slots: []`, `slots_stale: true`, `total_slots: 3`, `available_slots: 1`, an owner lease and a live dispatched pane dispatches into the free slot(s) (per-slot mode is not entered on stale/empty data).
2. A count-based multi-slot payload with spare `available_slots` and a held lease no longer blocks dispatch.
3. A count-based single-slot payload with a held lease still refuses (preserve WL-0MU8809SZ0022VZG AC3).
4. A contract test pins `slots_stale` parsing and the empty-array fallback.

## Notes

- Blocks the parent RCA's AC1 ("dispatches resume during agent runs").
- Child WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME's comment already anticipated this follow-up ("If cheap-mode responses also serve slots=[] ... perSlotMode is false and the stall persists").
